headword: {一挙両得|いっきょりょうとく}
gloss: two gains from one action; killing two birds with one stone

definitions.gloss: two gains from one action; killing two birds with one stone
definitions.explanation: A four-character idiom: a single action that brings two benefits at the same time.

examples.japanese: ⟦それ→それ：00994_sore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一挙両得|いっきょりょうとく}だ。
examples.english: That's two birds with one stone.

examples.japanese: {自転車通勤|じてんしゃつうきん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{運動|うんどう}→運動：00821_undou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧{一挙両得|いっきょりょうとく}だ。
examples.english: Cycling to work is good exercise too, so it's two gains in one.

examples.japanese: ⟦{海外|かいがい}→海外：00134_kaigai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦アルバイト→アルバイト：01528_arubaito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦すれば→する：00392_suru⟧、⟦お{金|かね}→お金：00611_okane⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{稼|かせ}ぎ→稼ぐ：02040_kasegu⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{語学|ごがく}→語学：02770_gogaku⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{学|まな}べて→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧{一挙両得|いっきょりょうとく}だ。
examples.english: Working part-time abroad lets you earn money and learn a language at the same time, so you get two benefits at once.

notes:
⟦{一挙|いっきょ}→一挙：11234_ikkyo⟧ (one action) + {両得|りょうとく} (gain on both counts). Usually used as a predicate: 〜⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一挙両得|いっきょりょうとく}だ, or as a modifier: {一挙両得|いっきょりょうとく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{方法|ほうほう}→方法：03621_houhou⟧ (a method that achieves two things at once).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{一石二鳥|いっせきにちょう}→一石二鳥：04764_issekinichou⟧: two birds with one stone — the same meaning and more common in conversation; it is a Japanese rendering of the English proverb
- ⟦{虻蜂取|あぶはちと}らず→虻蜂取らず：06293_abuhachitorazu⟧: chasing two things and getting neither — the opposite outcome
